prompt: Salaries (in \$1000) 10 years after graduation for 5 alumni from each of three schools — **RU: 31, 56, 143, 78, 210; PS: 30, 54, 37, 26, 70; UC: 22, 21, 24, 65, 36.** (1) Draw boxplots (median, quartiles, extremes); the ANOVA F-test p-value is 0.06 — interpret it via the boxplot. Are the samples skewed? Do they meet the F-test assumptions? (2) Use median and quartiles for a spread-vs-level plot; find the optimal power transformation. (3) Redo the ANOVA F-test after transformation.
solution: (1) The data are right-skewed and non-normal with unequal variances, so the ANOVA F-test assumptions fail; the boxplot shows a large difference favoring RU that the F-test (p = 0.06) cannot detect. (2) The spread-vs-level plot (log IQR vs log median) has slope between 1 and 1.5, suggesting a power transformation with power $1 - b$, i.e. between 0 (log) and $-0.5$. (3) After transformation the ANOVA F-test is significant (p $\approx 0.04$): the three schools' salaries differ.

prompt: July temperatures (°F) on the same randomly chosen date in each of 7 years (2013–2019); measurements in different years are independent, but the two cities on the same day are not. **New Brunswick: 78, 81, 90, 85, 88, 83, 83; Piscataway: 78, 79, 90, 82, 87, 82, 81.** (A) Give point estimates of each city's mean July temperature and the standard errors. (B) Give a 95% prediction interval for next year's New Brunswick temperature. (C) Test whether the two cities' mean July temperatures are equal at level 0.05.
solution: (A) New Brunswick: mean 84, sd 4.08, SE $= 4.08/\sqrt7 = 1.54$. Piscataway: mean 82.71, sd 4.31, SE $= 1.63$. (B) $84 \pm t_{6,.975}\,s\sqrt{1+1/7} = 84 \pm 2.45(4.46) \approx (73.3, 94.7)$. (C) Because same-day measurements are paired/dependent, use a paired test on the 7 differences: mean difference 1.29, sd 1.11, SE $= 0.42$, $t = 1.29/0.42 = 3.07 > t_{6,.975} = 2.45$ — reject $H_0$; the city means differ.
